chapterLabels.5: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: The Epistle of Ignatius to the Tarsians Ignatius, who is also called Theophorus, to the Church which is at Tarsus, saved in Christ, worthy of praise, worthy of remembrance, and worthy of love: Mercy and peace from God the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ, be ever multiplied.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Chapter 1 — His own sufferings: exhortation to stedfastness.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: From Syria even unto Rome I fight with beasts: not that I am devoured by brute beasts, for these, as ye know, by the will of God, spared Daniel, but by beasts in the shape of men, in whom the merciless wild beast himself lies hid, and pricks and wounds me day by day.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: But none of these hardships "move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself," in such a way as to love it better than the Lord.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Wherefore I am prepared for encountering fire, wild beasts, the sword or the cross, so that only I may see Christ my Saviour and God, who died for me.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: I therefore, the prisoner of Christ, who am driven along by land and sea, exhort you: "stand fast in the faith," and be ye steadfast, "for the just shall live by faith;" be ye unwavering, for "the Lord causes those to dwell in a house who are of one and the same character".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Chapter 2 — Cautions against false doctrine.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: I have learned that certain of the ministers of Satan have wished to disturb you, some of them asserting that Jesus was born only in appearance, was crucified in appearance, and died in appearance; others that He is not the Son the Creator, and others that He is Himself God over all.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Others, again, hold that He is a mere man, and others that this flesh is not to rise again, so that our proper course is to live and partake of a life of pleasure, for that this is the chief good to beings who are in a little while to perish.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: A swarm of such evils has burst in upon us.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: But ye have not "given place by subjection to them, no, not for one hour".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: For ye are the fellow-citizens as well as the disciples of Paul, who "fully preached the Gospel from Jerusalem, and round about unto Illyricum," and bare about "the marks of Christ" in his flesh.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Chapter 3 — The true doctrine respecting Christ.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Mindful of him, do ye by all means know that Jesus the Lord was truly born of Mary, being made of a woman; and was as truly crucified.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: For, says he, "God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of the Lord Jesus".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: And He really suffered, and died, and rose again.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: For says Paul, "If Christ should become passible, and should be the first to rise again from the dead".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: And again, "In that He died, He died unto sin once: but in that He liveth, He liveth unto God".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Otherwise, what advantage would there be in becoming subject to bonds, if Christ has not died? what advantage in patience? what advantage in enduring stripes? And why such facts as the following: Peter was crucified; Paul and James were slain with the sword; John was banished to Patmos; Stephen was stoned to death by the Jews who killed the Lord? But, in truth, none of these sufferings were in vain; for the Lord was really crucified by the ungodly.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Chapter 4 — Continuation.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: And know ye, moreover, that He who was born of a woman was the Son of God, and He that was crucified was "the first-born of every creature," and God the Word, who also created all things.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: For says the apostle, "There is one God, the Father, of whom are all things; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: And again, "For there is one God, and one Mediator between God and man, the man Christ Jesus;" and, "By Him were all things created that are in heaven, and on earth, visible and invisible; and He is before all things, and by Him all things consist".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Chapter 5 — Refutation of the previously mentioned errors.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: And that He Himself is not God over all, and the Father, but His Son, He shows when He says, "I ascend unto my Father and your Father, and to my God and your God".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: And again, "When all things shall be subdued unto Him, then shall He also Himself be subject unto Him that put all things under Him, that God may be all in all".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Wherefore it is one Person who put all things under, and who is all in all, and another Person to whom they were subdued, who also Himself, along with all other things, becomes subject to the former.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Chapter 6 — Continuation.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Nor is He a mere man, by whom and in whom all things were made; for "all things were made by Him".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: "When He made the heaven, I was present with Him; and I was there with Him, forming the world along with Him, and He rejoiced in me daily".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: And how could a mere man be addressed in such words as these: "Sit Thou at My right hand?" And how, again, could such an one declare: "Before Abraham was, I am?" And, "Glorify Me with Thy glory which I had before the world was?" What man could ever say, "I came down from heaven, not to do Mine own will, but the will of Him that sent Me?" And of what man could it be said, "He was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world: He was in the world, and the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: He came unto His own, and His own received Him not?" How could such a one be a mere man, receiving the beginning of His existence from Mary, and not rather God the Word, and the only-begotten Son? For "in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: And in another place, "The Lord created Me, the beginning of His ways, for His ways, for His works.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Before the world did He found Me, and before all the hills did He beget Me".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Chapter 7 — Continuation.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: And that our bodies are to rise again, He shows when He says, "Verily I say unto you, that the hour cometh, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear the voice of the Son of God; and they that hear shall live".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: And says the apostle, "For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: And that we must live soberly and righteously, he shows when he says again, "Be not deceived: neither adulterers, nor effeminate persons, nor abusers of themselves with mankind, nor fornicators, nor revilers, nor drunkards, nor thieves, can inherit the kingdom of God".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: And again, "If the dead rise not, then is not Christ raised; our preaching therefore is vain, and your faith is also vain: ye are yet in your sins.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Then they also that are fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: If the dead rise not, let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we die".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: But if such be our condition and feelings, wherein shall we differ from asses and dogs, who have no care about the future, but think only of eating, and of indulging such appetites as follow after eating? For they are unacquainted with any intelligence moving within them.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Chapter 8 — Exhortations to holiness and good order.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: May I have joy of you in the Lord! Be ye sober.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Lay aside, every one of you, all malice and beast-like fury, evil-speaking, calumny, filthy speaking, ribaldry, whispering, arrogance, drunkenness, lust, avarice, vainglory, envy, and everything akin to these.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: "But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Ye presbyters, be subject to the bishop; ye deacons, to the presbyters; and ye, the people, to the presbyters and the deacons.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Let my soul be for theirs who preserve this good order; and may the Lord be with them continually!.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Chapter 9 — Exhortations to the discharge of relative duties.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Ye husbands, love your wives; and ye wives, your husbands.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Ye children, reverence your parents.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Ye parents, "bring up your children in the nurture and admonition of the Lord".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Honour those who continue in virginity, as the priestesses of Christ; and the widows that persevere in gravity of behaviour, as the altar of God.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Ye servants, wait upon your masters with respectful fear.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Ye masters, issue orders to your servants with tenderness.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Let no one among you be idle; for idleness is the mother of want.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: I do not enjoin these things as being a person of any consequence, although I am in bonds for Christ; but as a brother, I put you in mind of them.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: The Lord be with you!.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Chapter 10 — Salutations.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: May I enjoy your prayers! Pray ye that may attain to Jesus.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: I commend unto you the Church which is at Antioch.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: The Churches of Philippi, whence also I write to you, salute you.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Philo, your deacon, to whom also I give thanks as one who has zealously ministered to me in all things, salutes you.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Agathopus, the deacon from Syria, who follows me in Christ, salutes you.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: "Salute ye one another with a holy kiss".

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: I salute you all, both male and female, who are in Christ.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: Fare ye well in body, and soul, and in one Spirit; and do not ye forget me.

1.label: Epistle to the Tarsians
1.text: The Lord be with you!.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: The Epistle of Ignatius to the Antiochians Ignatius, who is also called Theophorus, to the Church sojourning in Syria, which has obtained mercy from God, and been elected by Christ, and which first received the name Christ, wishes happiness in God the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 1 — Cautions against error.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: The Lord has rendered my bonds light and easy since I learnt that you are in peace, that you live in all harmony both of the flesh and spirit.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: "I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you, that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called," guarding against those heresies of the wicked one which have broken in upon us, to the deceiving and destruction of those that accept of them; but that ye give heed to the doctrine of the apostles, and believe both the law and the prophets: that ye reject every Jewish and Gentile error, and neither introduce a multiplicity of gods, nor yet deny Christ under the pretence of maintaining the unity of God.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 2 — The true doctrine respecting God and Christ.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: For Moses, the faithful servant of God, when he said, "The Lord thy God is one Lord," and thus proclaimed that there was only one God, did yet forthwith confess also our Lord when he said, "The Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah fire and brimstone from the Lord".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: And again, "And God said, Let Us make man after our image: and so God made man, after the image of God made He him".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: And further "In the image of God made He man".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: And that the Son of God was to be made man Moses shows when he says, "A prophet shall the Lord raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 3 — The same continued.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: The prophets also, when they speak as in the person of God, saying, "I am God, the first of beings, and I am also the last, and besides Me there is no God," concerning the Father of the universe, do also speak of our Lord Jesus Christ.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: "A Son," they say, has been given to us, on whose shoulder the government is from above; and His name is called the Angel of great counsel, Wonderful, Counsellor, the strong and mighty God".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: And concerning His incarnation, "Behold, a virgin shall be with Child, and shall bring forth a Son; and they shall call his name Immanuel".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: And concerning the passion, "He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; and as a lamb before her shearers is dumb, I also was an innocent lamb led to be sacrificed".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 4 — Continuation.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: The Evangelists, too, when they declared that the one Father was "the only true God," did not omit what concerned our Lord, but wrote: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: The same was in the beginning with God.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: All things were made by Him, and without Him was not anything made that was made".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: And concerning the incarnation: "The Word," says the Scripture, "became flesh, and dwelt among us".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: And again: "The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: And those very apostles, who said "that there is one God," said also that "there is one Mediator between God and men".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Nor were they ashamed of the incarnation and the passion.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: For what says one? "The man Christ Jesus, who gave Himself" for the life and salvation of the world.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 5 — Denunciation of false teachers.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Whosoever, therefore, declares that there is but one God, only so as to take away the divinity of Christ, is a devil, and an enemy of all righteousness.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: He also that confesseth Christ, yet not as the Son of the Maker of the world, but of some other unknown being, different from Him whom the law and the prophets have proclaimed, this man is an instrument of the devil.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: And he that rejects the incarnation, and is ashamed of the cross for which I am in bonds, this man is antichrist.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Moreover, he who affirms Christ to be a mere man is accursed, according to the declaration of the prophet, since he puts not his trust in God, but in man.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Wherefore also he is unfruitful, like the wild myrtle-tree.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 6 — Renewed cautions.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: These things I write to you, thou new olive-tree of Christ, not that I am aware you hold any such opinions, but that I may put you on your guard, as a father does his children.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Beware, therefore, of those that hasten to work mischief, those "enemies of the cross of Christ, whose end is destruction, whose glory is in their shame".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Beware of those "dumb dogs," those trailing serpents, those scaly dragons, those asps, and basilisks, and scorpions.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: For these are subtle wolves, and apes that mimic the appearance of men.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 7 — Exhortation to consistency of conduct.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Ye have been the disciples of Paul and Peter; do not lose what was committed to your trust.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Keep in remembrance Euodias, your deservedly-blessed pastor, into whose hands the government over you was first entrusted by the apostles.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Let us not bring disgrace upon our Father.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Let us prove ourselves His true-born children, and not bastards.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Ye know after what manner I have acted among you.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: The things which, when present, I spoke to you, these same, when absent, I now write to you.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: "If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Be ye followers of me.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: My soul be for yours, when I attain to Jesus.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Remember my bonds.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 8 — Exhortations to the presbyters and others.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Ye presbyters, "feed the flock which is among you," till God shall show who is to hold the rule over you.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: For "I am now ready to be offered," that I "may win Christ".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Let the deacons know of what dignity they are, and let them study to be blameless, that they may be the followers of Christ.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Let the people be subject to the presbyters and the deacons.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Let the virgins know to whom they have consecrated themselves.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 9 — Duties of husbands, wives, parents, and children.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Let the husbands love their wives, remembering that, at the creation, one woman, and not many, was given to one man.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Let the wives honour their husbands, as their own flesh; and let them not presume to address them by their names.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Let them also be chaste, reckoning their husbands as their only partners, to whom indeed they have been united according to the will of God.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Ye parents, impart a holy training to your children.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Ye children, "honour your parents, that it may be well with you".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 10 — Duties of masters and servants.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Ye masters, do not treat your servants with haughtiness, but imitate patient Job, who declares, "I did not despise the cause of my man-servant, or of my maid-servant, when they contended with me.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: For what in that case shall I do when the Lord makes an inquisition regarding me?" And you know what follows.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Ye servants, do not provoke your masters to anger in anything, lest ye become the authors of incurable mischiefs to yourselves.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 11 — Inculcation of various moral duties.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Let no one addicted to idleness eat, lest he become a wanderer about, and a whoremonger.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Let drunkenness, anger, envy, reviling, clamour, and blasphemy "be not so much as named among you".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Let not the widows live a life of pleasure, lest they wax wanton against the word.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Be subject to Caesar in everything in which subjection implies no spiritual danger.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Provoke not those that rule over you to wrath, that you may give no occasion against yourselves to those that seek for it.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: But as to the practice of magic, or the impure love of boys, or murder, it is superfluous to write to you, since such vices are forbidden to be committed even by the Gentiles.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: I do not issue commands on these points as if I were an apostle; but, as your fellow-servant, I put you in mind of them.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 12 — Salutations.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: I salute the holy presbytery.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: I salute the sacred deacons, and that person most dear to me, whom may I behold, through the Holy Spirit, occupying my place when I shall attain to Christ.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: My soul be in place of his.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: I salute the sub-deacons, the readers, the singers, the doorkeepers, the labourers, the exorcists, the confessors.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: I salute the keepers of the holy gates, the deaconesses in Christ.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: I salute the virgins betrothed to Christ, of whom may I have joy in the Lord Jesus.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: I salute the people of the Lord, from the smallest to the greatest, and all my sisters in the Lord.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 13 — Salutations continued.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: I salute Cassian and his partner in life, and their very dear children.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Polycarp, that most worthy bishop, who is also deeply interested in you, salutes you; and to him I have commended you in the Lord.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: The whole Church of the Smyrnaeans, indeed, is mindful of you in their prayers in the Lord.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Onesimus, the pastor of the Ephesians, salutes you.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Damas, the bishop of Magnesia, salutes you.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Polybius, bishop of the Trallians, salutes you.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Philo and Agathopus, the deacons, my companions, salute you, "Salute one another with a holy kiss".

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: Chapter 14 — Conclusion.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: I write this letter to you from Philippi.

2.label: Epistle to the Antiochians
2.text: May He who is alone unbegotten, keep you stedfast both in the spirit and in the flesh, through Him who was begotten before time began! And may I behold you in the kingdom of Christ! I salute him who is to bear rule over you in my stead: may I have joy of him in the Lord! Fare ye well in God, and in Christ, being enlightened by the Holy Spirit.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: The Epistle of Ignatius to Hero, a Deacon of Antioch Ignatius, who is also called Theophorus, to Hero, the deacon of Christ, and the servant of God, a man honoured by God, and most dearly loved as well as esteemed, who carries Christ and the Spirit within him, and who is mine own son in faith and love: Grace, mercy, and peace from Almighty God, and from Christ Jesus our Lord, His only-begotten Son, "who gave Himself for our sins, that He might deliver us from the present evil world," and preserve us unto His heavenly kingdom.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Chapter 1 — Exhortations to earnestness and moderation.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: I Exhort thee in God, that thou add speed to thy course, and that thou vindicate thy dignity.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Have a care to preserve concord with the saints.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Bear the burdens of the weak, that "thou mayest fulfil the law of Christ".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Devote thyself to fasting and prayer, but not beyond measure, lest thou destroy thyself thereby.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Do not altogether abstain from wine and flesh, for these things are not to be viewed with abhorrence, since the Scripture saith, "Ye shall eat the good things of the earth".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: And again, "Ye shall eat flesh even as herbs".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: And again, "Wine maketh glad the heart of man, and oil exhilarates, and bread strengthens him".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: But all are to be used with moderation, as being the gifts of God.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: "For who shall eat or who shall drink without Him? For if anything be beautiful, it is His; and if anything be good, it is His".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Give attention to reading, that thou mayest not only thyself know the laws, but mayest also explain them to others, as the earnest servant of God.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: "No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life, that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier; and if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned except he strive lawfully".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: I that am in bonds pray that my soul may be in place of yours.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Chapter 2 — Cautions against false teachers.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Every one that teaches anything beyond what is commanded, though he be deemed worthy of credit, though he be in the habit of fasting, though he live in continence, though he work miracles, though he have the gift of prophecy, let him be in thy sight as a wolf in sheep's clothing, labouring for the destruction of the sheep.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: If any one denies the cross, and is ashamed of the passion, let him be to thee as the adversary himself.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: "Though he gives all his goods to feed the poor, though he remove mountains, though he give his body to be burned," let him be regarded by thee as abominable.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: If any one makes light of the law or the prophets, which Christ fulfilled at His coming, let him be to thee as antichrist.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: If any one says that the Lord is a mere man, he is a Jew, a murderer of Christ.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Chapter 3 — Exhortations as to ecclesiastical duties.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: "Honour widows that are widows indeed".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Be the friend of orphans; for God is "the Father of the fatherless, and the Judge of the widows".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Do nothing without the bishops; for they are priests, and thou a servant of the priests.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: They baptize, offer sacrifice, ordain, and lay on hands; but thou ministerest to them, as the holy Stephen did at Jerusalem to James and the presbyters.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Do not neglect the sacred meetings of the saints; inquire after every one by name.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: "Let no man despise thy youth, but be thou an example to the believers, both in word and conduct".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Chapter 4 — Servants and women are not to be despised.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Be not ashamed of servants, for we possess the same nature in common with them.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Do not hold women in abomination, for they have given thee birth, and brought thee up.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: It is fitting, therefore, to love those that were the authors of our birth (but only in the Lord), inasmuch as a man can produce no children without a woman.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: It is right, therefore, that we should honour those who have had a part in giving us birth.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: "Neither is the man without the woman, nor the woman without the man," except in the case of those who were first formed.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: For the body of Adam was made out of the four elements, and that of Eve out of the side of Adam.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: And, indeed, the altogether peculiar birth of the Lord was of a virgin alone.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: This took place not as if the lawful union of man and wife were abominable, but such a kind of birth was fitting to God.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: For it became the Creator not to make use of the ordinary method of generation, but of one that was singular and strange, as being the Creator.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Chapter 5 — Various relative duties.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Flee from haughtiness, "for the Lord resisteth the proud".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Abhor falsehood, for says the Scripture, "Thou shalt destroy all them that speak lies".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Guard against envy, for its author is the devil, and his successor Cain, who envied his brother, and out of envy committed murder.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Exhort my sisters to love God, and be content with their own husbands only.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: In like manner, exhort my brethren also to be content with their own wives.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Watch over the virgins, as the precious treasures of Christ.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Be long-suffering, that thou mayest be great in wisdom.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Do not neglect the poor, in so far as thou art prosperous.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: For "by alms and fidelity sins are purged away".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Chapter 6 —Exhortations to purity and caution.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Keep thyself pure as the habitation of God.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Thou art the temple of Christ.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Thou art the instrument of the Spirit.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Thou knowest in what way I have brought thee up.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Though I am the least of men, do thou seek to follow me, be thou an imitator of my conduct.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: I do not glory in the world, but in the Lord.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: I exhort Hero, my son; "but let him that glorieth, glory in the Lord".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: May I have joy of thee, my dear son, whose guardian may He be who is the only unbegotten God, and the Lord Jesus Christ! Do not believe all persons, do not place confidence in all; nor let any man get the better of thee by flattery.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: For many are the ministers of Satan; and "he that is hasty to believe is light of heart".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Chapter 7 — Solemn charge to Hero, as future bishop of Antioch.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Keep God in remembrance, and thou shalt never sin.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Be not double-minded in thy prayers; for blessed is he who doubteth not.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: For I believe in the Father of the Lord Jesus Christ, and in His only-begotten Son, that God will show me, Hero, upon my throne.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Add speed, therefore, to thy course.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: I charge thee before the God of the universe, and before Christ, and in the presence of the Holy Spirit, and of the ministering ranks of angels, keep in safety that deposit which I and Christ have committed to thee, and do not judge thyself unworthy of those things which have been shown by God to me concerning thee.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: I hand over to thee the Church of Antioch.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: I have commended you to Polycarp in the Lord Jesus Christ.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Chapter 8 — Salutations.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: The bishops, Onesimus, Bitus, Damas, Polybius, and all they of Philippi (whence also I have written to thee), salute thee in Christ.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Salute the presbytery worthy of God: salute my holy fellow-deacons, of whom may I have joy in Christ, both in the flesh and in the spirit.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Salute the people of the Lord, from the smallest to the greatest, every one by name; whom I commit to thee as Moses did the Israelites to Joshua, who was their leader after him.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: And do not reckon this which I have said presumptuous on my part; for although we are not such as they were, yet we at least pray that we may be so, since indeed we are the children of Abraham.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Be strong, therefore, O Hero, like a hero, and like a man.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: For from henceforth thou shalt lead in and out the people of the Lord that are in Antioch, and so "the congregation of the Lord shall not be as sheep which have no shepherd".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Chapter 9 — Concluding salutations and instructions.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Salute Cassian, my host, and his most serious-minded partner in life, and their very dear children, to whom may "God grant that they find mercy of the Lord in that day," on account of their ministrations to us, whom also I commend to thee in Christ.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Salute by name all the faithful in Christ that are at Laodicea.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Do not neglect those at Tarsus, but look after them steadily, confirming them in the Gospel.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: I salute in the Lord, Maris the bishop of Neapolis, near Anazarbus.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: Salute thou also Mary my daughter, distinguished both for gravity and erudition, as also "the Church which is in her house".

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: May my soul be in place of hers: she is the very pattern of pious women.

3.label: Epistle to Hero
3.text: May the Father of Christ, by His only-begotten Son, preserve thee in good health, and of high repute in all things, to a very old age, for the benefit of the Church of God! Farewell in the Lord, and pray thou that I may be perfected.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: The Epistle of Ignatius to the Philippians Ignatius, who is also called Theophorus, to the Church of God which is at Philippi, which has obtained mercy in faith, and patience, and love unfeigned: Mercy and peace from God the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ, "who is the Saviour of all men, specially of them that believe".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 1 — Reason for writing the epistle.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Being mindful of your love and of your zeal in Christ, which ye have manifested towards us, we thought it fitting to write to you, who display such a godly and spiritual love to the brethren, to put you in remembrance of your Christian course, "that ye all speak the same thing, being of one mind, thinking the same thing, and walking by the same rule of faith," as Paul admonished you.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For if there is one God of the universe, the Father of Christ, "of whom are all things;" and one Lord Jesus Christ, our Lord, "by whom are all things;" and also one Holy Spirit, who wrought in Moses, and in the prophets and apostles; and also one baptism, which is administered that we should have fellowship with the death of the Lord; and also one elect Church; there ought likewise to be but one faith in respect to Christ.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For "there is one Lord, one faith, one baptism; one God and Father of all, who is through all, and in all".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 2 — Unity of the three divine persons.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: There is then one God and Father, and not two or three; One who is; and there is no other besides Him, the only true God.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For "the Lord thy God," saith the Scripture, "is one Lord".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And again, "Hath not one God created us? Have we not all one Father? And there is also one Son, God the Word.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For "the only-begotten Son," saith the Scripture, "who is in the bosom of the Father".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And again, "One Lord Jesus Christ".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And in another place, "What is His name, or what His Son's name, that we may know?" And there is also one Paraclete.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For "there is also," saith the Scripture, "one Spirit," since "we have been called in one hope of our calling".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And again, "We have drunk of one Spirit," with what follows.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And it is manifest that all these gifts possessed by believers "worketh one and the self-same Spirit".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: There are not then either three Fathers, or three Sons, or three Paracletes, but one Father, and one Son, and one Paraclete.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Wherefore also the Lord, when He sent forth the apostles to make disciples of all nations, commanded them to "baptize in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost," not unto one person having three names, nor into three persons who became incarnate, but into three possessed of equal honour.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 3 — Christ was truly born, and died.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For there is but One that became incarnate, and that neither the Father nor the Paraclete, but the Son only, who became so not in appearance or imagination, but in reality.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For "the Word became flesh".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For "Wisdom builded for herself a house".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And God the Word was born as man, with a body, of the Virgin, without any intercourse of man.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For it is written, "A virgin shall conceive in her womb, and bring forth a son".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: He was then truly born, truly grew up, truly ate and drank, was truly crucified, and died, and rose again.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: He who believes these things, as they really were, and as they really took place, is blessed.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: He who believeth them not is no less accursed than those who crucified the Lord.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For the prince of this world rejoiceth when any one denies the cross, since he knows that the confession of the cross is his own destruction.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For that is the trophy which has been raised up against his power, which when he sees, he shudders, and when he hears of, is afraid.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 4 — The malignity and folly of Satan.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And indeed, before the cross was erected, he (Satan) was eager that it should be so; and he "wrought" for this end "in the children of disobedience".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: He wrought in Judas, in the Pharisees, in the Sadducees, in the old, in the young, and in the priests.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: But when it was just about to be erected, he was troubled, and infused repentance into the traitor, and pointed him to a rope to hang himself with, and taught him to die by strangulation.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: He terrified also the silly woman, disturbing her by dreams; and he, who had tried every means to have the cross prepared, now endeavoured to put a stop to its erection; not that he was influenced by repentance on account of the greatness of his crime (for in that case he would not be utterly depraved), but because he perceived his own destruction to be at hand.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For the cross of Christ was the beginning of his condemnation, the beginning of his death, the beginning of his destruction.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Wherefore, also, he works in some that they should deny the cross, be ashamed of the passion, call the death an appearance, mutilate and explain away the birth of the Virgin, and calumniate the human nature itself as being abominable.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: He fights along with the Jews to a denial of the cross, and with the Gentiles to the calumniating of Mary, who are heretical in holding that Christ possessed a mere phantasmal body.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For the leader of all wickedness assumes manifold forms, beguiler of men as he is, inconsistent, and even contradicting himself, projecting one course and then following another.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For he is wise to do evil, but as to what good may be he is totally ignorant.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And indeed he is full of ignorance, on account of his voluntary want of reason: for how can he be deemed anything else who does not perceive reason when it lies at his very feet?.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 5 — Apostrophe to Satan.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For if the Lord were a mere man, possessed of a soul and body only, why dost thou mutilate and explain away His being born with the common nature of humanity? Why dost thou call the passion a mere appearance, as if it were any strange thing happening to a mere man? And why dost thou reckon the death of a mortal to be simply an imaginary death? But if, on the other hand, He is both God and man, then why dost thou call it unlawful to style Him "the Lord of glory," who is by nature unchangeable? Why dost thou say that it is unlawful to declare of the Lawgiver who possesses a human soul, "The Word was made flesh," and was a perfect man, and not merely one dwelling in a man? But how came this magician into existence, who of old formed all nature that can be apprehended either by the senses or intellect, according to the will of the Father; and, when He became incarnate, healed every kind of disease and infirmity?.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 6 — Continuation.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And how can He be but God, who raises up the dead, sends away the lame sound of limb, cleanses the lepers, restores sight to the blind, and either increases or transmutes existing substances, as the five loaves and the two fishes, and the water which became wine, and who puts to flight thy whole host by a mere word? And why dost thou abuse the nature of the Virgin, and style her members disgraceful, since thou didst of old display such in public processions, and didst order them to be exhibited naked, males in the sight of females, and females to stir up the unbridled lust of males? But now these are reckoned by thee disgraceful, and thou pretendest to be full of modesty, thou spirit of fornication, not knowing that then only anything becomes disgraceful when it is polluted by wickedness.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: But when sin is not present, none of the things that have been created are shameful, none of them evil, but all very good.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: But inasmuch as thou art blind, thou revilest these things.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 7 — Continuation: inconsistency of Satan.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And how, again, does Christ not at all appear to thee to be of the Virgin, but to be God over all, and the Almighty? Say, then, who sent Him? Who was Lord over Him? And whose will did He obey? And what laws did He fulfil, since He was subject neither to the will nor power of any one? And while you deny that Christ was born, you affirm that the unbegotten was begotten, and that He who had no beginning was nailed to the cross, by whose permission I am unable to say.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: But thy changeable tactics do not escape me, nor am I ignorant that thou art wont to walk with slanting and uncertain steps.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And thou art ignorant who really was born, thou who pretendest to know everything.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 8 — Continuation: ignorance of Satan.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For many things are unknown to thee; such as the following: the virginity of Mary; the wonderful birth; Who it was that became incarnate; the star which guided those who were in the east; the Magi who presented gifts; the salutation of the archangel to the Virgin; the marvellous conception of her that was betrothed; the announcement of the boy-forerunner respecting the son of the Virgin, and his leaping in the womb on account of what was foreseen; the songs of the angels over Him that was born; the glad tidings announced to the shepherds; the fear of Herod lest his kingdom should be taken from him; the command to slay the infants; the removal into Egypt, and the return from that country to the same region; the infant swaddling-bands; the human registration; the nourishing by means of milk; the name of father given to Him who did not beget; the manger because there was not room elsewhere; no human preparation for the Child; the gradual growth, human speech, hunger, thirst, journeyings, weariness; the offering of sacrifices and then also circumcision, baptism; the voice of God over Him that was baptized, as to who He was and whence He had come; the testimony of the Spirit and the Father from above; the voice of John the prophet when it signified the passion by the appellation of "the Lamb;" the performance of divers miracles, manifold healings; the rebuke of the Lord ruling both the sea and the winds; evil spirits expelled; thou thyself subjected to torture, and, when afflicted by the power of Him who had been manifested, not having it in thy power to do anything.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 9 — Continuation: ignorance of Satan.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Seeing these things, thou wast in utter perplexity.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And thou wast ignorant that it was a virgin that should bring forth; but the angels' song of praise struck thee with astonishment, as well as the adoration of the Magi, and the appearance of the star.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Thou didst revert to thy state of wilful ignorance, because all the circumstances seemed to thee trifling; for thou didst deem the swaddling-bands, the circumcision, and the nourishment by means of milk contemptible: these things appeared to thee unworthy of God.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Again, thou didst behold a man who remained forty days and nights without tasting human food, along with ministering angels at whose presence thou didst shudder, when first of all thou hadst seen Him baptized as a common man, and knewest not the reason thereof.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: But after His lengthened fast thou didst again assume thy wonted audacity, and didst tempt Him when hungry, as if He had been an ordinary man, not knowing who He was.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For thou saidst, "If thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Now, this expression, "If thou be the Son," is an indication of ignorance.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For if thou hadst possessed real knowledge, thou wouldst have understood that the Creator can with equal ease both create what does not exist, and change that which already has a being.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And thou temptedst by means of hunger Him who nourisheth all that require food.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And thou temptedst the very "Lord of glory," forgetting in thy malevolence that "man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For if thou hadst known that He was the Son of God, thou wouldst also have understood that He who had kept his body from feeling any want for forty days and as many nights, could have also done the same for ever.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Why, then, does He suffer hunger? In order to prove that He had assumed a body subject to the same feelings as those of ordinary men.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: By the first fact He showed that He was God, and by the second that He was also man.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 10 — Continuation: audacity of Satan.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Darest thou, then, who didst fall "as lightning" from the very highest glory, to say to the Lord, "Cast thyself down from hence to Him to whom the things that are not are reckoned as if they were, and to provoke to a display of vainglory Him that was free from all ostentation? And didst thou pretend to read in Scripture concerning Him: "For He hath given His angels charge concerning Thee, and in their hands they shall bear Thee up, lest thou shouldest dash Thy foot against a stone?" At the same time thou didst pretend to be ignorant of the rest, furtively concealing what the Scripture predicted concerning thee and thy servants: "Thou shalt tread upon the adder and the basilisk; the lion and the dragon shall thou trample under foot".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 11 — Continuation: audacity of Satan.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: If, therefore, thou art trodden down under the feet of the Lord, how dost thou tempt Him that cannot be tempted, forgetting that precept of the lawgiver, "Thou shall not tempt the Lord thy God?" Yea, thou even darest, most accursed one, to appropriate the works of God to thyself, and to declare that the dominion over these was delivered to thee.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And thou dost set forth thine own fall as an example to the Lord, and dost promise to give Him what is really His own, if He would fall down and worship thee.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: And how didst thou not shudder, O thou spirit more wicked through thy malevolence than all other wicked spirits, to utter such words against the Lord? Through thine appetite wast thou overcome, and through thy vainglory wast thou brought to dishonour: through avarice and ambition dost thou now draw on others to ungodliness.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Thou, O Belial, dragon, apostate, crooked serpent, rebel against God, outcast from Christ, alien from the Holy Spirit, exile from the ranks of the angels, reviler of the laws of God, enemy of all that is lawful, who didst rise up against the first-formed of men, and didst drive forth from obedience to the commandment of God those who had in no respect injured thee; thou who didst raise up against Abel the murderous Cain; thou who didst take arms against Job: dost thou say to the Lord, "If Thou wilt fall down and worship me?" Oh what audacity! Oh what madness! Thou runaway slave, thou incorrigible slave, dost thou rebel against the good Lord? Dost thou say to so great a Lord, the God of all that either the mind or the senses can perceive, "If Thou wilt fall down and worship me?".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 12 — The meek reply of Christ.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: But the Lord is long-suffering, and does not reduce to nothing him who in his ignorance dares to utter such words, but meekly replies, "Get thee hence, Satan".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: He does not say, "Get thee behind Me," for it is not possible that he should be converted; but, "Begone, Satan," to the course which thou hast chosen.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: "Begone" to those things to which, through thy malevolence, thou hast been called.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For I know Who I am, and by Whom I have been sent, and Whom it behoves Me to worship.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: For "thou shall worship the Lord thy God, and Him only shalt thou serve".

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: I know the one God; I am acquainted with the only Lord from whom thou hast become an apostate.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: I am not an enemy of God; I acknowledge His pre-eminence; I know the Father, who is the author of my generation.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 13 — Various exhortations and directions.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: These things, brethren, out of the affection which I entertain for you, I have felt compelled to write, exhorting you with a view to the glory of God, not as if I were a person of any consequence, but simply as a brother.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Be ye subject to the bishop, to the presbyters, and to the deacons.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Love one another in the Lord, as being the images of God.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Take heed, ye husbands, that ye love your wives as your own members.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Ye wives also, love your husbands, as being one with them in virtue of your union.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: If any one lives in chastity or continence, let him not be lifted up, lest he lose his reward.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Do not lightly esteem the festivals.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Despise not the period of forty days, for it comprises an imitation of the conduct of the Lord.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: After the week of the passion, do not neglect to fast on the fourth and sixth days, distributing at the same time of thine abundance to the poor.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: If any one fasts on the Lord's Day or on the Sabbath, except on the paschal Sabbath only, he is a murderer of Christ.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 14 — Farewells and cautions.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Let your prayers be extended to the Church of Antioch, whence also I as a prisoner am being led to Rome.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: I salute the holy bishop Polycarp; I salute the holy bishop Vitalius, and the sacred presbytery, and my fellow-servants the deacons; in whose stead may my soul be found.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Once more I bid farewell to the bishop, and to the presbyters in the Lord.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: If any one celebrates the passover along with the Jews, or receives the emblems of their feast, he is a partaker with those that killed the Lord and His apostles.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Chapter 15 — Salutations.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Conclusion.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Philo and Agathopus the deacons salute you.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: I salute the company of virgins, and the order of widows; of whom may I have joy! I salute the people of the Lord, from the least unto the greatest.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: I have sent you this letter through Euphanius the reader, a man honoured of God, and very faithful, happening to meet with him at Rhegium, just as he was going on board ship.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Remember my bonds that I may be made perfect in Christ.

4.label: Epistle to the Philippians
4.text: Fare ye well in the flesh, the soul, and the spirit, while ye think of things perfect, and turn yourselves away from the workers of iniquity, who corrupt the word of truth, and are strengthened inwardly by the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: The Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius Mary of Cassobelae to Ignatius Maria, a proselyte of Jesus Christ, to Ignatius Theophorus, most blessed bishop of the apostolic Church which is at Antioch, beloved in God the Father, and Jesus: Happiness and safety.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: We all beg for thee joy and health in Him.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: Chapter 1 — Occasion of the epistle.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: Since Christ has, to our wonder, been made known among us to be the Son of the living God, and to have become man in these last times by means of the Virgin Mary, of the seed of David and Abraham, according to the announcements previously made regarding Him and through Him by the company of the prophets, we therefore beseech and entreat that, by thy wisdom, Maris our friend, bishop of our native Neapolis, which is near Zarbus, and Eulogius, and Sobelus the presbyter, be sent to us, that we be not destitute of such as preside over the divine word as Moses also says, "Let the Lord God look out a man who shall guide this people, and the congregation of the Lord shall not be as sheep which have no shepherd".

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: Chapter 2 — Youth may be allied with piety and discretion.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: But as to those whom we have named being young men, do not, thou blessed one, have any apprehension.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: For I would have you know that they are wise about the flesh, and are insensible to its passions, they themselves glowing with all the glory of a hoary head through their own intrinsic merits, and though but recently called as young men to the priesthood.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: Now, call thou into exercise thy thoughts through the Spirit that God has given to thee by Christ, and thou wilt remember that Samuel, while yet a little child, was called a seer, and was reckoned in the company of the prophets, that he reproved the aged Eli for transgression, since he had honoured his infatuated sons above God the author of all things, and had allowed them to go unpunished, when they turned the office of the priesthood into ridicule, and acted violently towards thy people.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: Chapter 3 — Examples of youthful devotedness.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: Moreover, the wise Daniel, while he was a young man, passed judgment on certain vigorous old man, showing them that they were abandoned wretches, and not worthy to be reckoned elders, and that, though Jews by extraction, they were Canaanites in practice.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: And Jeremiah, when on account of his youth he declined the office of a prophet entrusted to him by God, was addressed in these words: "Say not, I am a youth; for thou shalt go to all those to whom I send thee, and thou shalt speak according to all that I command thee; because I am with thee".

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: And the wise Solomon, when only in the twelfth year of his age, had wisdom to decide the important question concerning the children of the two women, when it was unknown to whom these respectively belonged; so that the whole people were astonished at such wisdom in a child, and venerated him as being not a mere youth, but a full-grown man.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: And he solved the hard questions of the queen of the Ethiopians, which had profit in them as the streams of the Nile have fertility, in such a manner that that woman, though herself so wise, was beyond measure astonished.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: Chapter 4 — The same subject continued.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: Josiah also, beloved of God, when as yet he could scarcely speak articulately, convicts those who were possessed of a wicked spirit as being false in their speech, and deceivers of the people.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: He also reveals the deceit of the demons, and openly exposes those that are no gods; yea, while yet an infant he slays their priests, and overturns their altars, and defiles the place where sacrifices were offered with dead bodies, and throws down the temples, and cuts down the groves, and breaks in pieces the pillars, and breaks open the tombs of the ungodly, that not a relic of the wicked might any longer exist.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: To such an extent did he display zeal in the cause of godliness, and prove himself a punisher of the ungodly, while he as yet faltered in speech like a child.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: David, too, who was at once a prophet and a king, and the root of our Saviour according to the flesh, while yet a youth is anointed by Samuel to be king.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: For he himself says in a certain place, "I was small among my brethren, and the youngest in the house of my father".

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: Chapter 5 — Expressions of respect for Ignatius.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: But time would fail me if I should endeavour to enumerate all those that pleased God in their youth, having been entrusted by God with either the prophetical, the priestly, or the kingly office.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: And those which have been mentioned may suffice, by way of bringing the subject to thy remembrance.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: But I entreat thee not to reckon me presumptuous or ostentatious in writing as I have done.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: For I have set forth these statements, not as instructing thee, but simply as suggesting the matter to the remembrance of my father in God.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: For I know my own place, and do not compare myself with such as you.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: I salute thy holy clergy, and thy Christ-loving people who are ruled under thy care as their pastor.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: All the faithful with us salute thee.

5.label: Epistle of Maria the Proselyte to Ignatius
5.text: Pray, blessed shepherd, that I may be in health as respects God.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: The Epistle of Ignatius to Mary at Neapolis, Near Zarbus.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Ignatius, who is also called Theaphorus, to her who has obtained mercy through the grace of the most high God the Father, and Jesus Christ the Lord, who died for us, to Mary, my daughter, most faithful, worthy of God, and bearing Christ in her heart, wishes abundance of happiness in God.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Chapter 1 — Acknowledgment of her excellence and wisdom.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Sight indeed is better than writing, inasmuch as, being one of the company of the senses, it not only, by communicating proofs of friendship, honours him who receives them, but also, by those which it in turn receives, enriches the desire for better things.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: But the second harbour of refuge, as the phrase runs, is the practice of writing, which we have received, as a convenient haven, by thy faith, from so great a distance, seeing that by means of a letter we have learned the excellence that is in thee.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: For the souls of the good, O thou wisest of women! resemble fountains of the purest water; for they allure by their beauty passers-by to drink of them, even though these should not be thirsty.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: And thy intelligence invites us, as by a word of command, to participate in those divine draughts which gush forth so abundantly in thy soul.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Chapter 2 — His own condition.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: But I, O thou blessed woman, not being now so much my own master as in the power of others, am driven along by the varying wills of many adversaries, being in one sense in exile, in another in prison, and in a third in bonds.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: But I pay no regard to these things.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Yea, by the injuries inflicted on me through them, I acquire all the more the character of a disciple, that I may attain to Jesus Christ.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: May I enjoy the torments which are prepared for me, seeing that "the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us".

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Chapter 3 — He had complied with her request.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: I have gladly acted as requested in thy letter, having no doubt respecting those persons whom thou didst prove to be men of worth.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: For I am sure that thou barest testimony to them in the exercise of a godly judgment, and not through the influence of carnal favour.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: And thy numerous quotations of Scripture passages exceedingly delighted me, which, when I had read, I had no longer a single doubtful thought respecting the matter.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: For I did not hold that those things were simply to be glanced over by my eyes, of which I had received from thee such an incontrovertible demonstration.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: May I be in place of thy soul, because thou lovest Jesus, the Son of the living God.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Wherefore also He Himself says to thee, "I love them that love Me; and those that seek Me shall find peace".

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Chapter 4 — Commendation and exhortation.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Now it occurs to me to mention, that the report is true which I heard of thee whilst thou wast at Rome with the blessed father Linus, whom the deservedly-blessed Clement, a hearer of Peter and Paul, has now succeeded.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: And by this time thou hast added a hundred-fold to thy reputation; and may thou, O woman! still further increase it.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: I greatly desired to come unto you, that I might have rest with you; but "the way of man is not in himself".

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: For the military guard under which I am kept hinders my purpose, and does not permit me to go further.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Nor indeed, in the state I am now in, can I either do or suffer anything.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Wherefore deeming the practice of writing the second resource of friends for their mutual encouragement, I salute thy sacred soul, beseeching of thee to add still further to thy vigour.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: For our present labour is but little, while the reward which is expected is great.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Chapter 5 — Salutations and good wishes.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Avoid those that deny the passion of Christ, and His birth according to the flesh: and there are many at present who suffer under this disease.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: But it would be absurd to admonish thee on other points, seeing that thou art perfect in every good work and word, and able also to exhort others in Christ.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Salute all that are like-minded with thyself, and who hold fast to their salvation in Christ.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: The presbyters and deacons, and above all the holy Hero, salute thee.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: Cassian my host salutes thee, as well as my sister, his wife, and their very dear children.

6.label: Epistle to Mary at Neapolis
6.text: May the Lord sanctify thee for evermore in the enjoyment both of bodily and spiritual health, and may I see thee in Christ obtaining the crown!.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: The Epistle of Ignatius to Saint John the Apostle Ignatius, and the brethren who are with him, to John the holy presbyter.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: We are deeply grieved at thy delay in strengthening us by thy addresses and consolations.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: If thy absence be prolonged, it will disappoint many of us.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: Hasten then to come, for we believe that it is expedient.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: There are also many of our women here, who are desirous to see Mary the mother of Jesus, and wish day by day to run off from us to you, that they may meet with her, and touch those breasts of hers which nourished the Lord Jesus, and may inquire of her respecting some rather secret matters.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: But Salome also, the daughter of Anna, whom thou lovest, who stayed with her five months at Jerusalem, and some other well-known persons, relate that she is full of all graces and all virtues, after the manner of a virgin, fruitful in virtue and grace.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: And, as they report, she is cheerful in persecutions and afflictions, free from murmuring in the midst of penury and want, grateful to those that injure her, and rejoices when exposed to troubles: she sympathizes with the wretched and the afflicted as sharing in their afflictions, and is not slow to come to their assistance.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: Moreover, she shines forth gloriously as contending in the fight of faith against the pernicious conflicts of vicious principles or conduct.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: She is the lady of our new religion and repentance, and the handmaid among the faithful of all works of piety.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: She is indeed devoted to the humble, and she humbles herself more devotedly than the devoted, and is wonderfully magnified by all, while at the same time she suffers detraction from the Scribes and Pharisees.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: Besides these points, many relate to us numerous other things regarding her.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: We do not, however, go so far as to believe all in every particular; nor do we mention such to thee.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: But, as we are informed by those who are worthy of credit, there is in Mary the mother of Jesus an angelic purity of nature allied with the nature of humanity.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: And such reports as these have greatly excited our emotions, and urge us eagerly to desire a sight of this (if it be lawful so to speak) heavenly prodigy and most sacred marvel.

7.label: First Epistle to St. John
7.text: But do thou in haste comply with this our desire; and fare thou well, Amen.

8.label: Second Epistle to St. John
8.text: A Second Epistle of Ignatius to Saint John.

8.label: Second Epistle to St. John
8.text: His friend Ignatius to John the holy presbyter.

8.label: Second Epistle to St. John
8.text: If thou wilt give me leave, I desire to go up to Jerusalem, and see the faithful saints who are there, especially Mary the mother, whom they report to be an object of admiration and of affection to all.

8.label: Second Epistle to St. John
8.text: For who would not rejoice to behold and to address her who bore the true God from her own womb, provided he is a friend of our faith and religion? And in like manner I desire to see the venerable James, who is surnamed Just, whom they relate to be very like Christ Jesus in appearance, in life, and in method of conduct, as if he were a twin-brother of the same womb.

8.label: Second Epistle to St. John
8.text: They say that, if I see him, I see also Jesus Himself, as to all the features and aspect of His body.

8.label: Second Epistle to St. John
8.text: Moreover, I desire to see the other saints, both male and female.

8.label: Second Epistle to St. John
8.text: Alas! why do I delay? Why am I kept back? Kind teacher, bid me hasten to fulfil my wish, and fare thou well, Amen.

9.label: Epistle to the Virgin Mary
9.text: The Epistle of Ignatius to the Virgin Mary Her friend Ignatius to the Christ-bearing Mary.

9.label: Epistle to the Virgin Mary
9.text: Thou oughtest to have comforted and consoled me who am a neophyte, and a disciple of thy beloved John.

9.label: Epistle to the Virgin Mary
9.text: For I have heard things wonderful to tell respecting thy son Jesus, and I am astonished by such a report.

9.label: Epistle to the Virgin Mary
9.text: But I desire with my whole heart to obtain information concerning the things which I have heard from thee, who wast always intimate and allied with Him, and who wast acquainted with all His secrets.

9.label: Epistle to the Virgin Mary
9.text: I have also written to thee at another time, and have asked thee concerning the same things.

9.label: Epistle to the Virgin Mary
9.text: Fare thou well; and let the neophytes who are with me be comforted of thee, and by thee, and in thee, Amen.

10.label: Reply of the Blessed Virgin
10.text: Reply of the Blessed Virgin to this Letter.

10.label: Reply of the Blessed Virgin
10.text: The lowly handmaid of Christ Jesus to Ignatius, her beloved fellow-disciple.

10.label: Reply of the Blessed Virgin
10.text: The things which thou hast heard and learned from John concerning Jesus are true.

10.label: Reply of the Blessed Virgin
10.text: Believe them, cling to them, and hold fast the profession of that Christianity which thou hast embraced, and conform thy habits and life to thy profession.

10.label: Reply of the Blessed Virgin
10.text: Now I will come in company with John to visit thee, and those that are with thee.

10.label: Reply of the Blessed Virgin
10.text: Stand fast in the faith, and show thyself a man; nor let the fierceness of persecution move thee, but let thy spirit be strong and rejoice in God thy Saviour, Amen.
